title: Driving in Europe: Car Insurance Checks Before You Go
description: UK drivers don’t need a green card in the EU, but should still check foreign-use cover, breakdown, hire cars and documents. A pre-trip checklist.
h1: Driving in Europe: insurance checks before you go
intro: Planning a road trip to France, Spain or beyond? Your UK car insurance gives at least the legal minimum across the EU, but that may be less cover than you have at home.

image.alt: Ferry sailing on calm water with mountains behind

sections.html: Since 2 August 2021, UK drivers don’t need a motor insurance green card to drive their own insured vehicle in the EU, EEA, Switzerland, Andorra, Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. You may still need one for some other countries; GOV.UK has the current list.

sections.h2: Check what your policy covers abroad
sections.html:
• Is comprehensive cover extended abroad, or only third party?
  • For how many days per trip and per year?
  • Does breakdown cover include Europe?
  • Are you covered on the ferry or in the Channel Tunnel?

Ask your insurer to extend cover if needed before you travel.

Carry your driving licence, V5C logbook (or VE103 if the car is leased or hired), and insurance certificate. Display a UK sticker if your number plate doesn’t show the UK identifier. Some countries require equipment such as warning triangles or reflective jackets, and some cities have low-emission zones. Check before you go.

Hire cars come with basic insurance but often a high excess. Standalone excess reimbursement insurance can be cheaper than the rental desk’s option; read what it covers (tyres, windscreen, underside). For trip ideas, see our sister site TravelDeals.

faqs.q: Do I need a green card to drive in France?
faqs.a: Not for a UK-insured vehicle since August 2021. Carry your insurance certificate and check foreign-use cover.

faqs.q: Is my breakdown cover valid in Europe?
faqs.a: Only if it includes European cover. Many UK policies are UK-only by default.
